question.problem:
Let $f(x)$ be the $6$-periodic extension of the function $F(x)=6x$ defined on $[-3,3).$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of a series converging to the $6$-periodic extension of 

$$
G(x)=3{x}^{2}={\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$

The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
6x∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{36(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }{{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f$ is 
{{field-2}} 
on $R,$ we may integrate its Fourier series term-by-term to get

$$
3{x}^{2}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{{field-3}}\cdot {{field-4}}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $F(x)$ is an odd function. So, the Fourier series of its $2L$-periodic extension has the form

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{L}).
$$

In our case, $L=3$ and we are already given the coefficients ${b}_{n}$ for $n\ge 1.$ Thus, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{36(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

Now, notice that the function $F$ is continuous on $(-3,3).$ 
Therefore, the $6$-periodic extension $f$ is $\text{piecewise continuous}$ on $R,$ so we may integrate its Fourier series term-by-term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}6t\,\text{d}t & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{36(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi t}{3})\,\text{d}t \\ [3{t}^{2}]_{0}^{x} & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{36(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\cdot [-\frac{3}{n\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi t}{3})]_{0}^{x} \\ 3{x}^{2} & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{108(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\cdot (1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}))\end{aligned}
$$
